newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico left burns ballots in election protest.
newsitem.headline: Mexico left burns ballots in election protest.

text.p: Challenging results of Sunday's election, leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) members burned ballot papers in the southeastern state of Campeche, a party official said on Wednesday.
The conservative opposition party PAN also protested at preliminary figures showing the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) winning the Campeche city mayor's election.

Campeche, a poor state on the Yucatan peninsula that is home to most of Mexico's oil reserves, voted to elect a new governor, one of six such races held the same day Mexico had national congressional elections.

Alejandro Encinas, the senior PRD official in the state, said members of his party, joined by the PAN and the PT Workers' Party, burned ballots on Tuesday night in the town of Hecelchakan, 700 miles (1100 km) southeast of Mexico City.
PRD members also occupied electoral authority offices in the coastal town of Champoton, he said.
Opposition leaders in Campeche say they can prove irregularities in the July 6 election and want to reverse the early official results.
Jorge Vaqueiro, the PAN leader in Campeche, told Reuters his party had proof that its candidate had won the mayor's election in Campeche city, not the PRI.
"We want the will of the citizens to be respected, vote by vote," he said. "We don't want deception".
On Tuesday the PRD candidate for Campeche state governor Layda Sansores led 12,000 people through the streets of the state capital to protest at alleged fraud by the PRI.
Preliminary official results in Campeche indicated a victory for PRI gubernatorial candidate Antonio Gonzalez Curi with 99,513 votes to Sansores' 83,523.
Supporters chanted: "We want no more fraud" and "Campechans unite." Sansores promised the PRD would officially challenge the results of the governor's race.
PRI national president Humberto Roque Villanueva told a news conference he was "not worried about Layda Sansores's hysterics."

The Campeche moves come after protests in the northern state of Sonora, where the conservative National Action Party (PAN) rejected early results showing its candidate Enrique Salgado Bojorquez losing the governor's race.

Salgado issued a statement alleging the PRI had used dirty tricks to win. "It is impossible to accept, that in a state where the opposition governs 84 percent of the municipalities, the PRI claims it won the gubernatorial race....Besides, the PRI lost its majority in the state congress and lost every race for federal congress, according to the results," he said.
